# opencode-copilot [![GitHub Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/andyzasl/opencode-copilot?color=blue&logo=github)](https://github.com/andyzasl/opencode-copilot/releases) [![OpenCode v2](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCode-v2-10b981?logo=terminal&logoColor=white)](https://opencode.ai) [![Security & Quality](https://github.com/andyzasl/opencode-copilot/actions/workflows/security.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/andyzasl/opencode-copilot/actions/workflows/security.yml) [![Dependencies](https://img.shields.io/badge/dependencies-0%20runtime-success)](package.json) [![Security Policy](https://img.shields.io/badge/security-audited-success?logo=github)](SECURITY.md) [![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-strict-3178C6?logo=typescript&logoColor=white)](tsconfig.json) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) An [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) v2 TUI plugin that shows your remaining GitHub Copilot quota and real-time chat usage directly in the sidebar **Context** block.

``` Context 9,234 tokens 45% used $0.12 spent Copilot ← this plugin 74% left (185k credits) Chat: 2.5 credits ``` The block renders dynamically when the active session is running on a `github-copilot` model. ## Features - **Billing Cycle Balance**: Displays remaining premium quota as both a percentage and total volume (credits or requests). - **Per-Chat Usage Attribution**: Tracks baseline balance upon session view and shows how much was consumed during the conversation (`Chat: X credits`). - **Plan Auto-detection**: Automatically adapts units based on Copilot's response (`credits` for token-metered plans, `requests` for discrete plans, or hides cleanly if unlimited). - **Zero Configuration**: Reads existing Copilot credentials from OpenCode's internal store automatically. - **Privacy & Security Focused**: Deliberately reads *only* the `github-copilot` OAuth token from OpenCode's local storage. Never falls back to general-purpose `GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GH_TOKEN` environment variables to prevent accidental credential leakage to undocumented endpoints. ## What the Numbers Mean Copilot plans report quota differently: | Plan reports | Unit shown | Example | |---|---|---| | `token_based_billing: true` | credits | `74% left (185k credits)` | | `token_based_billing: false` | requests | `82% left (247 requests)` | | `unlimited: true` | *hidden* | — | The line below (`Chat: ...`) displays the change in quota observed since the current session was opened. ## Installation ### Option 1 — OpenCode CLI (Recommended) Install the plugin directly from GitHub into your global OpenCode configuration: ```bash opencode plugin add andyzasl/opencode-copilot ``` ### Option 2 — Global Config (`opencode.json`) Add the repository specifier to your `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`: ```json { "plugin": [ "andyzasl/opencode-copilot" ] } ``` ### Option 3 — Local or Manual Configuration (`tui.json`) If you cloned this repository locally: ```bash git clone git@github.com:andyzasl/opencode-copilot.git cd opencode-copilot npm install ``` Reference the source directly in `~/.config/opencode/tui.json` (or `.opencode/tui.json` for project-local): ```json { "plugin": ["/path/to/opencode-copilot/src/tui.tsx"] } ``` ## Authentication Authentication is completely automatic. The plugin checks the `github-copilot` OAuth access token in OpenCode's `auth.json` across standard OS storage paths: 1. `$XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/auth.json` 2. macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/opencode/auth.json` 3. Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%/opencode/auth.json` and `%APPDATA%/opencode/auth.json` 4. Linux / Fallback: `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` If you are not authenticated with Copilot in OpenCode, nothing is rendered. ## Security & Credential Transparency Because OpenCode plugins run directly in the host user environment without sandboxing, this plugin is built according to community security best practices: - 🔒 **Narrow Credential Scope**: The plugin *only* reads the `github-copilot` OAuth access token from OpenCode's internal `auth.json`. It **never** reads environment variables (`GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GH_TOKEN`), preventing broad personal access tokens or CI credentials from being sent. - 🚫 **No Credential Persistence**: The token is read on-demand directly from disk and discarded immediately after the HTTP call. It is never cached in memory, written to files, or logged. - 🌐 **Single Trusted Host**: The only outbound destination is `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/user`. Zero third-party telemetry, trackers, or foreign network calls. - 🛡️ **Zero Runtime Dependencies**: The package contains zero external dependencies. The entire codebase is a single file ([`src/tui.tsx`](src/tui.tsx), < 200 lines) easily auditable in under 2 minutes. - ⚡ **Passive & Safe**: No agent tools registered (`tool.execute`), no shell command execution, and no prompt interception. If any network or API error occurs, the plugin degrades silently without disrupting your session. See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for the complete threat model and security guarantees. ## Polling & Network Behavior | Aspect | Detail | |---|---| | **Endpoint** | `api.github.com/copilot_internal/user` | | **Refresh Interval** | Every 5 minutes while active, plus on `session.idle` (5 s throttle) | | **Rate Limiting** | Minimum 30 s gap between background polls; enforces single in-flight request | | **Timeout** | 5 seconds | | **Idle Behavior** | Background polling starts only after a Copilot session is observed | | **Degradation** | Fails silently without cluttering the UI with error banners | > [!NOTE] > `copilot_internal/user` is an internal GitHub API endpoint. If GitHub modifies or restricts this endpoint, the plugin safely hides rather than throwing unhandled exceptions. ## Development & Verification Check types: ```bash npm install npm run typecheck ``` Continuous integration runs TypeScript typechecking, dependency audits (`npm audit`), secret detection (Gitleaks), CodeQL SAST analysis, and Trivy filesystem vulnerability scanning on every pull request and push to `main`. ## License [MIT](LICENSE) © Andrei Zaslavskii

# Security & Threat Model

OpenCode plugins run within the user's host environment with full process privileges. Because OpenCode does not sandbox plugins by default, security, data privacy, and credential boundaries must be explicitly designed and verified.

This document describes the security guarantees, credential handling, and network profile of `@andyzasl/opencode-copilot`.

---

## 1. Credential & Token Boundary

### What the Plugin Reads
- **Only** the `github-copilot` OAuth access token entry in OpenCode's internal `auth.json`.
- The token is read on-demand directly from disk and discarded immediately after the HTTP request completes.
- It is never stored in persistent memory, cached to disk, or logged.

### What the Plugin Deliberately Does Not Do
- **No environment variable fallbacks (`GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GH_TOKEN`)**: Personal Access Tokens (PATs) and CI tokens frequently carry repository-wide write, workflow, or administrative scopes. This plugin will never read or transmit general-purpose environment tokens.
- **No key guessing**: Neighbouring keys in `auth.json` (such as OpenAI, Anthropic, or GitLab tokens) are never accessed.
- **No local credential retention**: If you run `opencode auth logout github-copilot` or rotate your credential, the token is revoked immediately.

---

## 2. Network Egress Profile

The plugin communicates strictly with GitHub's official infrastructure:

| Attribute | Specification |
|---|---|
| **Destination Host** | `api.github.com` (HTTPS, port 443) |
| **Endpoint** | `/copilot_internal/user` |
| **HTTP Method** | `GET` |
| **Payload** | None (headers only: `Authorization`, `Accept`, `X-GitHub-Api-Version`) |
| **Telemetry / Tracking** | Zero. No third-party endpoints, CDNs, or analytics services. |

### Network Inactivity
- **No background traffic on other providers**: Polling is completely suspended when working on non-Copilot sessions (Claude, OpenAI, Ollama, etc.).
- **Rate-limited**: Minimum 30-second interval between background requests; concurrency guard ensures only one in-flight request at any time.
- **Fail-safe timeout**: All requests enforce a 5-second timeout via `AbortSignal.timeout`.

---

## 3. Minimal Attack Surface

- **Zero Runtime Dependencies**: The package contains zero production dependencies (`dependencies` only contains `@types/node`). It relies entirely on the OpenCode host runtime.
- **Single-File Source**: The entire plugin logic resides in [`src/tui.tsx`](src/tui.tsx) (~190 lines of readable TypeScript), enabling complete line-by-line manual audit in under 2 minutes.
- **No Shell or File Execution**: The plugin registers no agent tools (`tool.execute`), executes no shell commands, modifies no files, and installs no prompt interception hooks.
- **Fail-Safe UI**: If the GitHub API fails, times out, or changes schema, the plugin degrades silently to absence rather than throwing errors or crashing the TUI.

---

## 4. Automated CI Security Scanning

Every commit and pull request is subjected to continuous automated scanning:

- **CodeQL (SAST)**: GitHub's semantic code analysis searching for injection, tainted input, and security bugs.
- **Gitleaks**: Scans git commit history for credentials and secrets.
- **Trivy**: Scans filesystem and dependency trees for CVEs and misconfigurations.
- **npm audit**: Audits dependencies for high/critical security advisories.

---

## 5. Reporting a Security Vulnerability

If you discover a security concern or potential vulnerability, please report it privately:

- Use GitHub's private vulnerability reporting feature on this repository: **Security > Report a vulnerability**.
- Or contact the maintainer directly at `andy.evil@gmail.com`.

Reports will be acknowledged within 48 hours and investigated promptly.
